title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page): for an auxiliary 'ring' A, Grothendieck has defined, for each integer N, a ring scheme D_N (written as a double-struck D, transcribed as O) over a base S_0, presumably Spec Z. Its unit group D_N^* is a commutative group scheme, and the D_N form a projective system. Writing Ẑ_0 for the profinite ring Ẑ taken as a constant pro-scheme over S_0, he sets (1+NZ)^* = {λ | 1+Nλ invertible}. He then looks at the reduction maps D_N^* -> D_1^* = Ẑ_0^*. The kernel is {1+Nλ | Nλ = 0}. As a bare scheme this is the N-torsion of the additive group, i.e. Spec Z[x]/(Nx).

This page continues that discussion.
- The kernel is a group scheme that is not flat when N ≠ 1 (the 'plat' in the transcription should most likely read 'non plat'). It is zero over Z[1/N]. Its fibres at primes p | N are the whole additive group: Z[x]/(Nx) ⊗ F_p = F_p[x]. So the image's '≃ G.' should probably read G_a, not G_m.
- He remarks that this amounts to choosing a section of D_N^* that is computed group-theoretically and reduces matters to the additive group.
- He specialises to N = 12, giving the extension (78)/(79): 1 -> (1+12Z)^* -> D_12^* -> (Z/12Z)^*_{S_0} -> 1. Here (Z/12Z)^* ≅ (Z/4)^* × (Z/6)^* ≅ μ × μ with μ = {±1}. The two sign characters are ε_2 (residue mod 4) and ε_3 (residue mod 6, equivalently mod 3).
- These characters are encoded by locally constant functions ν_2, ν_3 with values in the constant scheme {0,1}_{S_0}, via the bijection 1 ↦ 0, −1 ↦ 1. So ε_i = (−1)^{ν_i} = 1 − 2ν_i, and the ν_i are idempotent functions.

The next page completes the computation.
- A set-theoretic (not homomorphic) section is μ_0 = (−5)^{ν_2} · 5^{ν_3}.
- Because the ν are idempotent, 5^ν = 1 + 4ν and (−5)^ν = 1 − 6ν, so μ_0 = 1 + 4ν_3 − 6ν_2 − 24ν_2ν_3.
- A general section of D_12^* is μ_0 times a factor [1+12λ_0].

Purpose: an explicit coordinatisation of the level-12 unit group scheme as 'sign data' (a finite constant part) times a congruence part. This is presumably for later use with 12-related structures (the abelianisation of SL_2(Z), μ_12, the Teichmüller and modular material of the Longue Marche), though the page itself does not say why 12 is chosen.
errors: Arithmetic checks out: −5 ≡ 3 mod 4 and ≡ 1 mod 3; 5 ≡ 1 mod 4 and ≡ 2 mod 3; the idempotent identities 5^ν = 1+4ν and (−5)^ν = 1−6ν hold; the product expansion is correct.
The fibres of the kernel {λ : Nλ = 0} at p | N should be the additive group G_a, not G_m. Either the handwriting is ambiguous or this is a slip.
The kernel Spec Z[x]/(Nx) is not flat for N ≠ 1. The transcription 'plat si N≠1' should most likely read 'non plat'.

ideas.what: Treat profinite unit groups Ẑ^* and congruence quotients as (pro-)group schemes over Spec Z; the reduction kernel is the non-flat group scheme ker(N: G_a -> G_a)
ideas.modern_name: Non-flat finite-type group schemes; N-torsion of G_a over Z
ideas.where_published: Group-scheme generalities in SGA 3; this specific D_N construction is not known to be published

ideas.what: Encode the sign characters of (Z/12)^* ≅ μ×μ by idempotent functions ν with ε = 1 − 2ν, and write a set-theoretic section (−5)^{ν_2}5^{ν_3} as a polynomial in the idempotents
ideas.modern_name: Locally constant / idempotent coordinates on constant group schemes; explicit cocycle section

ideas.what: Special attention to level N = 12 for the unit group scheme D_N^*
ideas.modern_name: Level-12 structure; μ_12 and the abelianisation of SL_2(Z)
ideas.where_published: The role of 12 appears in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche, but not in this form

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a projective system of ring schemes D_N with unit groups D_N^* over S_0. He explicitly declines to study the system or its projective limits in general (previous page) and only treats N = 12 by hand. The general structure of this 'scheme-theoretic Ẑ' tower is left open on the page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is a scheme-theoretic packaging of profinite congruence data that may relate to arithmetic models of Ẑ-modules in his Galois–Teichmüller programme. On this page alone it is routine computation.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct but routine computation: a non-flat N-torsion kernel and an explicit section of a level-12 unit extension using idempotent sign coordinates. The only mildly interesting feature is the scheme-theoretic treatment of Ẑ^* at level 12 within the Longue Marche sequel; nothing here appears to be a new result.
transcription_corrections: 'les fibres en les p|N sont ≃ G_m' most likely reads '≃ G_a' (the symbol in the image is G followed by a small subscript).
'(... plat si N≠1)' is likely '(non plat si N≠1)'.
The ring symbol is a double-struck D (D_N, D_12), consistent with the neighbouring pages, not O.
'pour se rapporter [?] à G_m' at the end of the paragraph likely also refers to G_a (the additive group scheme).
